attempts.summary: Configured node1 (OpenWrt) to publish node2's private-network HTTP service (10.10.10.2:8080) on node1's management address port 80, reachable by node3, while keeping the service itself off the management network. Set up: static private-link addressing (node1 eth1=10.10.10.1/24, node2 eth1=10.10.10.2/24), a systemd-managed Python HTTP service on node2 bound only to 10.10.10.2:8080 (not 0.0.0.0), a firewalld rule on node2 opening 8080/tcp for the private zone, and on node1 a new UCI firewall zone 'priv' (eth1) with a DNAT redirect (lan:80 -> priv:10.10.10.2:8080) plus masquerade on the priv zone so return traffic routes back through node1 (fixing an initial routing asymmetry where node2 replied directly to node3, bypassing node1). Verified node3 can reach the service via node1:80 and cannot reach node2:8080 directly. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol for all three nodes: captured pre-restart boot_id/uptime baselines, triggered native reboot on each node sequentially, polled until exec access returned, confirmed changed boot_id + reset uptime on each, and re-verified full service recovery (private IPs, demo-http.service active, firewalld port open, end-to-end curl through node1 returning 200, direct 8080 access still blocked) after each restart.
